# Churchill Downs News Release: Kentucky Derby Week Tickets On Sale Thursday at Noon


## Nov 19, 2026


Tickets for all Kentucky Derby Week special events at Churchill Downs will go on sale Thursday at 12 p.m. ET at https://www.kentuckyderby.com/visit/derby-week-events/.


The seven-day Kentucky Derby Week will span Saturday, April 24 (Opening Day of the 44-day Spring Meet) and culminate with the 153rd running of the $5 million Kentucky Derby presented by Woodford Reserve (Grade I) on Saturday, May 1.


Kentucky Derby Week special events include:


Opening Weekend Saturday (Saturday, April 24) – Derby Week officially begins with a full day of live racing and family-friendly entertainment, highlighted by the 2027 Kentucky Derby and Kentucky Oaks Post Position Draws presented by Ford. New for 2027, Opening Weekend Saturday will feature special opening ceremonies and a limited-edition pennant available during a jockey autograph signing. Guests can also enjoy interactive horse racing experiences, family activities, photo opportunities with the Derby Trophy and replica Garland, and the return of the Style Under the Spires fashion contest where guests can showcase their Coordinated Classics.
Opening Weekend Sunday (Sunday, April 25) – Opening Weekend continues with live racing, brunch and entertainment for a relaxed and social Sunday at Churchill Downs. Guests can enjoy brunch options in dining rooms and at select concessions around the track, brunch-inspired cocktails, live music and interactive experiences throughout the track, creating a fun way for friends and families to gather and continue the excitement of Derby Week.
Dawn at the Downs Dining (Monday, April 26) – A cherished Derby Week tradition, Dawn at the Downs offers guests an up-close look at Kentucky Derby and Kentucky Oaks contenders during their exclusive morning training window while enjoying a buffet breakfast overlooking the historic racetrack. Guests can watch the contenders complete their final preparations for the first weekend in May from the Stakes Room or Millionaires Row, with dining packages starting at $55. Gates open at 7 a.m., with morning training continuing until 10 a.m., notwithstanding renovation breaks.
Community Shopping Day (Monday, April 26) – Community Shopping Day returns, where the Kentucky Derby store located at the Clubhouse Gate will be open to the public from 6:45 a.m. to 12 p.m. A ticket is not required to shop at the Kentucky Derby Store Clubhouse location. Guests should enter at the Clubhouse Gate.
502’sDay (Tuesday, April 27) – 502’sDay celebrates the people, culture and creativity that make Louisville one-of-a-kind. In partnership with the Louisville Independent Business Alliance (LIBA), the day will bring the city’s “Keep Louisville Weird” spirit to Churchill Downs with local artists, independent businesses and interactive experiences inspired by Louisville’s distinctive neighborhoods. Guests are encouraged to Shop Local and showcase looks from Louisville-area shops and designers during the Style Under the Spires fashion contest. General Admission is $10 in advance and $15 on event day.
Winsday: Great Thrills for the Greater Good (Wednesday, April 28) – “Winsday” returns to shine a spotlight on Louisville’s robust nonprofit community. In partnership with the Community Foundation of Louisville, local nonprofit organizations will be invited to fundraise and highlight the work they do to make Louisville a more vibrant place to live, work and play. By purchasing tickets through partner nonprofits, guests will directly contribute to these vital agencies, with a portion of each ticket sale benefiting their incredible work. The Charity Post Draw and auxiliary drawings provide additional opportunities to support participating nonprofits. Guests are encouraged to wear Bold Patterns for the Style Under the Spires fashion contest.
Thurby presented by Old Forester (Thursday, April 29) – In partnership with Frazier Kentucky History Museum, Thurby celebrates the people, places and traditions that make the Commonwealth iconic. Guests can experience Kentucky-inspired entertainment throughout the day, including roving representations of famous Kentuckians and cultural icons presented by Actors Theatre of Louisville, a look at Old Forester’s storied bourbon legacy and the return of the Style Under the Spires fashion contest, where guests are encouraged to showcase their best Vintage-Inspired looks.
Taste of Derby (Thursday, April 29) – Immerse yourself in the excitement of the Kentucky Derby with exclusive access to Derby Experiences’ Taste of Derby Party. Spend an evening savoring gourmet creations from celebrity chefs, sipping craft cocktails and enjoying live music in an electric atmosphere. This one-of-a-kind celebration is the perfect way to kick off Derby Weekend, combining Louisville’s vibrant food scene with an exciting first taste of the festivities ahead.
Derby Week general admission tickets are $34 on Opening Weekend Saturday, Opening Weekend Sunday and Winsday; $54 on Thurby; and a special $10 general admission offering for advance 502’sDay purchases with $15 event day general admission. Reserved box seats range from $44-$49 for Opening Saturday, Opening Sunday and Winsday and $70-$110 for Thurby depending on the location.


A limited number of options remain in Dining and Suite areas for groups of 12 or more by contacting the Groups Team at (502) 636-4450 or groupsales@kyderby.com.


Tickets for the 153rd Kentucky Oaks and Kentucky Derby on April 30-May 1 are available by visiting https://am.ticketmaster.com/churchill/buy and www.DerbyExperiences.com or by calling the Kentucky Derby Ticket Sales Team at (502) 636-4447. Tickets for Taste of Derby on Thursday, April 29 are available by visiting www.DerbyExperiences.com. For more information or details on experiences go to www.KentuckyDerby.com.


Churchill Downs also provides a secure, official resale marketplace to purchase Derby and Oaks tickets via the Churchill Downs Ticketmaster Ticket Exchange on www.KentuckyDerby.com.


ABOUT THE KENTUCKY DERBY


The $5 million Kentucky Derby takes place on the first Saturday in May at historic Churchill Downs in Louisville, Ky. Inaugurated in 1875, the legendary 1 ¼-mile race for 3-year-old Thoroughbreds is the longest continually held annual sporting event in the United States and the first leg of the Thoroughbred Championship Series. Also known as “The Run for the Roses” and “The Most Exciting Two Minutes in Sports,” the Kentucky Derby is the most attended horse race in the nation. The 153rd Kentucky Derby will take place on Saturday, May 1, 2027. For more information, please visit www.KentuckyDerby.com.


ABOUT CHURCHILL DOWNS RACETRACK


Churchill Downs Racetrack (“CDRT”), the world’s most legendary racetrack, has been the home of The Kentucky Derby, the longest continually held annual sporting event in the United States, since 1875. Located in Louisville, CDRT features a series of themed race days during Derby Week, including the Kentucky Oaks, and conducts Thoroughbred horse racing during three race meets in the Spring, September and Fall. Additionally, it is the home of premier races in the Thoroughbred Championship Series. CDRT is located on 175 acres and has a one-mile dirt track, a 7/8-mile turf track, a stabling area, and provides seating for approximately 60,000 guests. The stable area has barns sufficient to accommodate 1,400 horses and a 114-room dormitory for backstretch personnel. CDRT also has a year-round simulcast wagering facility. www.ChurchillDowns.com.
